src.label: FASFC (Belgian food safety agency) — rabies and travelling with pets

head: Dogs, cats and ferrets from outside the EU need a microchip, rabies vaccination and an EU-model certificate.
lines: The FASFC says a pet coming to Belgium from a non-EU country must always carry a microchip, be vaccinated against rabies, and have either an EU pet passport or a health certificate drawn up to the EU model by an official vet in the country of departure, depending on where it comes from.
Vaccination is possible from 12 weeks of age; after a first vaccination the animal may cross the border 21 days later at the earliest, and a vaccination given before the microchip does not count.

Depending on the country of origin a blood test must also show the vaccine worked: if the blood sample is taken in the third country, travel to the EU is allowed only 3 months after sampling, while a test done in the EU before leaving is valid at once with no waiting period.
